title: Deep-Learning-Aided Detection of Mycobacteria in Pathology Specimens Increases the Sensitivity in Early Diagnosis of Pulmonary Tuberculosis Compared with Bacteriology Tests
study_context: Ziehl-Neelsen acid-fast-bacillus detection using CNN training with two pulmonary tuberculosis autopsy cases and forty AFB-negative biopsy cases.
population_or_data: Ziehl-Neelsen acid-fast-bacillus detection using CNN training with two pulmonary tuberculosis autopsy cases and forty AFB-negative biopsy cases.
task: Ziehl-Neelsen acid-fast-bacillus detection using CNN training with two pulmonary tuberculosis autopsy cases and forty AFB-negative biopsy cases.
main_findings: Two tuberculosis autopsy cases supplied annotated positive acid-fast bacilli, and forty AFB-negative biopsy cases supplied background/artifact examples for CNN training, followed by application to bronchoscopy specimens.
limitations: Selected-page review only; not a full-paper audit. Text and rendered pages 1, 2 checked on 2026-10-07.

Bacillus detection is not cardiac rejection grading. The source ties positive training material to autopsy and negative material to biopsy; it does not eliminate specimen-source confounding or establish the benefit of adding autopsy data over a matched biopsy-only baseline. Methods 2.1 mentions 14 validation cases whereas the abstract reports 42; no validation sample-size or efficacy claim is indexed.
does_not_establish: Bacillus detection is not cardiac rejection grading. relevance_to_project: A concrete noncardiac precedent for transferring lesion-level information from autopsy tissue to biopsy analysis.
